newsitem.title: USA: Foster Wheeler exec hopeful for incinerator bill.
newsitem.headline: Foster Wheeler exec hopeful for incinerator bill.

text.p: An executive with Foster Wheeler Corp. said Wednesday the company was working to get a bill that would restore a state subsidy to a waste-to-energy incinerator in Illinois through the legislature.

"All I can say is that we're working toward moving the bill through the House and hopefully it will receive approval and move onto the Senate," said Tom O'Brien, senior vice president and general counsel of the Clinton, N.J.-based company, which was the developer of an incinerator in the Chicago suburb of Robbins.
He declined to comment on how much support the company has lined up for the bill in the House.
The House Public Utilities Committee on Tuesday advanced the bill onto the House floor after hearing testimony from representatives from Foster Wheeler and a Chicago-based environmental group.
The measure has until April 25 to move out of the House, but is not expected to be taken up until after the Easter holiday.

The bill faces likely opposition from House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, and from Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar, who signed into law a year ago a repeal of a subsidy that guarenteed incinerators a higher rate at which they could sell the electricity they produced to utilities.
The subsidy's repeal imperiled nearly $500 million of tax-exempt, unrated bonds, including $320 million of debt sold for the Robbins project.
The bill would only restore the subsidy to Robbins and to a bond-financed incinerator in Ford Heights because both were financed, built and had received necessary government orders and permits.
Foster Wheeler and developers of three other incinerators have lawsuits pending in state courts challenging the subsidy's repeal.
